author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Damage to Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline could keep the system out of service for three to five weeks, officials briefed on the situation told The Associated Press.

The pipeline, which stretches about 1,200 kilometers across Saudi Arabia, carries crude from Gulf ports to Yanbu on the Red Sea. Authorities shut it down after an attack Thursday that Saudi Arabia blamed on drones launched by Iranian-backed militias in Iraq.

Officials said repairs may allow the line to operate partially, but they could not immediately say how much oil would continue moving during the work. The pipeline has recently carried an average of roughly 2.6 million to 4 million barrels per day, according to an analysis cited by AP.
The reported damage adds pressure to global oil logistics at a time when fighting and attacks are already affecting shipping routes around the Red Sea and nearby waterways.

NorthEast News is labeling the story developing because the repair timeline, pipeline capacity and responsibility for the attack could be revised as Saudi authorities and operators release more information.
dek: Damage to Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline may take three to five weeks to repair, according to officials briefed on the situation.
headline: Saudi oil pipeline could remain out of service for weeks after drone attack
